question.worked_solution:
We differentiate each component separately.

- For the $x$-component $x(t)=4{e}^{2(t-1)},$ we have

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=8{e}^{2(t-1)},
$$

and therefore,

$$
{x}^{′}(1)=8{e}^{0}=8.
$$

- For the $y$-component $y(t)=-6\operatorname{sin}⁡(t-1),$ we have

$$
{y}^{′}(t)=-6\operatorname{cos}⁡(t-1),
$$

and therefore,

$$
{y}^{′}(1)=-6\operatorname{cos}⁡(0)=-6.
$$

So, we conclude that

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(1) & =⟨{x}^{′}(1),\,{y}^{′}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨8,\,-6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, computing the magnitude of this vector, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}|{r}^{′}(1)| & =\sqrt{{8}^{2}+{(-6)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{64+36} \\  & =\sqrt{100} \\  & =10.\end{aligned}
$$
